text:
alice: Heads-up — saw a customer report where a client "seek"/rewind during a streaming session caused a toolcall to be re-executed and billed twice. small thread of logs attached. :thinking_face:

bob: Ugh. Seen similar for reconnects, but rewind/seek is new. Do you have the raw router/billing lines?

alice: pasted a minimal extract:
```
[router] ts=2026-11-02T14:02:31Z session=abc123 action=seek offset=-18 model=redwood-x tool_call_id=tc-9 resumed_from=seq=42
[serve] ts=2026-11-02T14:02:31Z session=abc123 invoked_tool=tc-9 response_tokens=38
[billing] ts=2026-11-02T14:02:32Z session=abc123 charge_token=PROTO100 provisional=true amount=38 reason=toolcall
[router] ts=2026-11-02T14:02:34Z session=abc123 resume_complete new_seq=60
[billing] ts=2026-11-02T14:02:35Z session=abc123 charge_token=PROTO101 provisional=false amount=38 reason=toolcall
```

carla: looks like we created a provisional charge when the resumed toolcall returned, and then later confirmed it as a separate charge instead of promoting the provisional entry. The provisional->confirmed path expects the same idempotency key but the seek path generates a new runtime id.

bob: So the core is idempotency key mismatch between pre-truncation and post-seek execution. We dedupe on tool_call_id + session but when a seek rewinds the stream we rewrite sequence numbers and reissue a new run id.

dan: Does this only happen when the client requests a negative offset (rewind) or also with forward-seek/clip?

alice: Customer did negative offset to re-render the last chunk, so rewind. Haven't seen forward-only.

eve: UX/console ask: we should surface provisional vs confirmed charges in the timeline and show "retry/seek" events that caused reexecution. Ops needs this to explain invoices.

carla: Suggestion: add a resume_id that the client supplies (or router synthesizes) and carry it through the toolcall ledger as the canonical idempotency key. If resume_id is present, promote any matching provisional row instead of creating a new charge.

bob: Agree. Also short-term mitigation: when we detect a seek within <G> seconds and same payload signature, suppress creating a new provisional entry and mark as "potential-dup" until confirmation window ends.

dan: That suppression sounds risky for concurrency. We'll need a clear telemetry tag so we can roll back quickly if we undercharge. Propose tagging events with resume.cause and resume.source fields.

infra-bot: deploy-checklist: add migration to backfill resume_id=null -> resume_id=<session> for recent provisional rows? File infra ticket for idempotency key change.

alice: I'll file a ticket with logs and minimal repro. action: eng-platform#4128 (add resume_id propagation + console flag).

eve: Also add a small console note: "If you used stream-rewind or client-side seek, billing may show provisional duplicates while we roll this out." Can we have that in next patch notes?

carla: Implementation sketch: router synthesizes resume_id = sha256(session + client_resume_nonce || inferred_seek_range). carry resume_id through to runner and billing. Billing: lookup provisional by resume_id + tool_call_sig; if exists, promote instead of insert. Add metric: billing.duplicate_seek_detected.

bob: Telemetry: add histogram of seek_offsets, and a counter seek_double_toolcall. Also emit event when provisional is promoted so console shows "provisional promoted" instead of duplicate charge.

dan: I'll prototype resume_id passthrough in the router this week. If anyone has objections to the key format speak now.

alice: no objections. thanks all. :thumbsup:

eve: filing a docs blurb for the console UX change.

infra-bot: created ticket infra/ttl-989 for DB backfill and safety checks.

alice: follow-up: will post repro + minimal client snippet tomorrow.
